reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows that a shear-induced ultra-nanocrystalline layer and dynamic amorphization occur during sliding in CoCrFeMnNi, supporting the mechanism. However, the key premise that thermal annealing (rather than sliding) can pre-form this layer is unsupported by the cited passages, and E3 concerns a different alloy system, providing no direct support.
premises: Thermal annealing of CoCrFeMnNi coatings can produce an ultra-nanocrystalline near-surface layer with grain sizes 10–50 nm.
An ultra-nanocrystalline layer in this alloy increases grain boundary area and promotes dynamic amorphization under sliding.
Dynamic amorphization blunts dislocation motion and accommodates plastic deformation, reducing wear and friction.
The inverse Hall-Petch behavior and low friction in CoCrFeMnNi are linked to a shear-induced ultra-nanocrystalline/amorphous layer.
